images.title: 16384 is 16 times 1024
images.purpose: Shows that 4 to the power 7 is 16 copies of 4 to the power 5, because their quotient is 4², which is 16.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text. One small square on the left and one large square made of a 4 by 4 grid of the same small squares on the right, with an arrow between.
images.exact_structure: Left: one teal (#0072B2) square, labelled '4⁵' above and '1024' below. Right: a large square made of exactly 16 identical teal (#0072B2) squares of the same size as the left square, in a 4 by 4 grid with thin white gaps, labelled '4⁷' above and '16384' below. Between them, a thick amber (#E69F00) arrow pointing right with the label '16 times' above it and '4² = 16' below it. Exactly 17 small squares, 1 arrow.

images.takeaway: To find how many times larger, divide the powers: subtract the exponents.
images.description: Shows that 4 to the power 7 is 16 copies of 4 to the power 5, because their quotient is 4², which is 16.
images.context: 16384 ÷ 1024 = 16 = 4². Also 4² is 4⁴ = 256 times 4 to the power −2.
images.teaching_notes: Ask how many times larger 4² is than 4 to the power −2.

image_decisions.why: The 16 copies make 'times larger' concrete as a quotient of powers, which is this concept.
